title: When LLMs Forget What They Believe: Characterizing State Integrity Collapse in Long-Horizon Dialogues
abstract: arXiv:2610.31314v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models can repeat an instruction while failing to keep obeying it. We study this recall-compliance dissociation in long-horizon dialogue and define State Integrity Collapse: a model preserves a stated constraint in memory but stops applying it to later turns. We introduce StateTrack-Bench, a controlled suite of conversations covering numerical, format, role/persona, factual-memory, and logical-rule constraints. Across seven provider-pinned model snapshots and five dialogue-depth probes, strict joint retention ranges from 62.4% to 100.0%, with degradation concentrated in symbolic constraints and in one especially brittle model. A forked recall audit shows that 88.6% of observed failures are behavioral-drift failures rather than ordinary forgetting; excluding the brittle outlier preserves this diagnosis (84.4% of failures). translated_title: 当大语言模型忘记自己所信奉的内容时：刻画长程对话中的状态完整性崩塌
translated_abstract: 大语言模型能够复述一条指令，却无法持续遵守它。我们在长程对话中研究了这种“记忆—服从分离”现象，并定义了“状态完整性崩塌”：模型在记忆中保留了已声明的约束，但在后续对话轮次中不再将其付诸执行。我们提出了StateTrack-Bench，这是一套受控的对话基准，涵盖数值、格式、角色/人设、事实记忆以及逻辑规则五类约束。在七个固定版本的模型快照和五个对话深度探测点上，严格的联合保持率介于62.4%至100.0%之间，且性能退化主要集中在符号类约束以及一个特别脆弱的模型上。一项分叉式记忆审计显示，88.6%的观测失败属于行为漂移失败，而非普通的遗忘；在排除该脆弱异常模型后，这一诊断依然成立（84.4%的失败）。在长达50轮对话深度的扩展评估进一步证实，这种分离现象在核心基准之外依然持续存在。
tldr: 该论文首次定义并量化了长程对话中的“状态完整性崩塌”现象——大语言模型虽在记忆中保留了约束却停止执行——并通过StateTrack-Bench基准与分叉式记忆审计证明，绝大多数失败（88.6%）是行为漂移而非普通遗忘。
en_tdlr: This paper defines and quantifies "State Integrity Collapse" in long-horizon dialogues—where LLMs retain stated constraints in memory but stop applying them—and introduces StateTrack-Bench with a forked recall audit showing that 88.6% of failures are behavioral drift rather than ordinary forgetting.
